extracted.intended_audience: aircraft operators, maintenance personnel, and stakeholders submitting comments on the FAA NPRM
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements associated with the FAA proposed Airworthiness Directive (NPRM) for Airbus Helicopters Model EC225LP, and instructions for submitting comments to the NPRM. Includes applicability, required maintenance/actions, compliance timing, recordkeeping, alternative methods, and procedural requirements for notice-and-comment participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments: most helpful content
rubrics_metrics.description: The most helpful comments reference a specific portion of the proposal, explain the reason for any recommended change, and include supporting data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission methods and docket
rubrics_metrics.description: You may send comments, using the procedures found in 14 CFR 11.43 and 11.45, by any of the following methods: Federal eRulemaking Portal (regulations.gov), Fax: (202) 493-2251, Mail: U.S. Department of Transportation, Docket Operations, M-30, West Building Ground Floor, Room W12-140, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, Washington, DC 20590, or Hand Delivery to the mail address above between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include “Docket No. FAA—2025—0909; Project Identifier MCAI—2023-00895-R” at the beginning of your comments. The AD docket can be examined at regulations.gov under Docket No. FAA—2025-0909 or in person at Docket Operations between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays. The AD docket contains this NPRM, the MCAI, any comments received, and other information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Business Information (CBI) designation
rubrics_metrics.description: CBI is commercial or financial information that is both customarily and actually treated as private by its owner and is exempt from public disclosure under FOIA (5 U.S.C. 552). If your comments contain CBI, clearly designate the submitted comments as CBI and mark each page containing CBI as 'PROPIN.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBI submissions will be treated as confidential and not placed in the public docket. Submissions containing CBI should be sent to Frank Huynh, Aviation Safety Engineer, FAA, 1600 Stewart Avenue, Suite 410, Westbury, NY 11590. Any commentary not specifically designated as CBI will be placed in the public docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability — affected helicopters/parts
rubrics_metrics.description: This AD applies to Airbus Helicopters Model EC225LP helicopters, certificated in any category, with the parts identified in paragraph (c)(1) or (2) of this AD installed, with 'XX' denoting any dash number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affected parts include: (1) MGB P/N 332A32-5001-XX, 332A32-5002-XX, or 332A32-5003-XX with a main reduction gear module and MOD 07-53016 installed (16-roller free wheel) and P/N 332A32-5011-XX, 332A32-5012-XX, or 332A32-5013-XX; and (2) MGB P/N 332A32-5004-XX with a main module P/N 332A32-5400-00.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsafe condition — wear on RH free wheel shaft
rubrics_metrics.description: This AD was prompted by a report of wear detected on the right-hand side (RH) free wheel shaft. The FAA is issuing this AD to prevent wear of the ramps of the RH free wheel shaft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not addressed, during an in-flight shutdown of the left-hand engine this unsafe condition could result in reduced ability to transfer one engine inoperative (OEI) power from the RH engine to the main rotor, and subsequent reduced control of the helicopter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance — timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine RH free wheel shaft TIS and replacement at 1,000 hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 hours time-in-service (TIS) after the effective date of this AD, determine the total hours TIS of the RH free wheel shaft since new or last RH free wheel shaft replacement during overhaul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the total hours TIS of the RH free wheel shaft is 1,000 or more hours TIS, before further flight, replace the MGB or replace the RH free wheel shaft. Thereafter, before any RH free wheel shaft accumulates 1,000 total hours TIS, replace the MGB or replace the RH free wheel shaft. If the total hours TIS is less than 1,000 hours TIS, replace before exceeding 1,000 hours TIS and thereafter before any RH free wheel shaft accumulates 1,000 total hours TIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Install placards: specifications and text
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 hours TIS after the effective date of this AD, install one or two self-adhesive placards on the instrument panel in full view of the pilot and co-pilot with 6-millimeter red letters on a white background that state the information contained in figure 1 to paragraph (g)(2)(i) of this AD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure text: 'The use of ENG1 “TRAINING IDLE” switch is prohibited. ENG2 “TRAINING IDLE” switch must be systematically used.' Note: Figure 4 of Airbus Helicopters Emergency Alert Service Bulletin No. EC225-04A016, Revision 4, dated June 19, 2023, shows an example of this placard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise Rotorcraft Flight Manual (RFM) and record entry
rubrics_metrics.description: After installing the required placard(s), before further flight, revise the limitations section of the existing Rotorcraft Flight Manual (RFM) for the helicopter by adding the information in figure 2 to paragraph (g)(2)(ii) of this AD, by inserting a copy of this AD, or by making pen-and-ink changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 2 text: 'The use of ENG1 “TRAINING IDLE” switch is prohibited. ENG2 “TRAINING IDLE” switch must be systematically used. Accomplishment of OEI training flight is allowed, provided that only ENG2 “TRAINING IDLE” switch is used for that purpose.' The owner/operator (pilot) holding at least a private pilot certificate may revise the existing RFM and must enter compliance with this RFM revision into the helicopter maintenance records in accordance with 14 CFR 43.9(a) and 14 CFR 91.417(a)(2)(v). The record must be maintained as required by 14 CFR 91.417, 121.380, or 135.439.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional terminating action — install alternate MGB configuration
rubrics_metrics.description: For Model EC225LP helicopters with parts identified in paragraph (c)(1) installed, as an optional terminating action for the requirements of this AD, install MGB P/N 332A32-5001-XX, 332A32-5002-XX, or 332A32-5003-XX with a main module (12-roller free wheel), without MOD 07-53016 installed, P/N 332A32-5011-XX, 332A32-5012-XX, or 332A32-5013-XX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Installation of these alternate MGB configurations terminates the AD requirements for those helicopters per the AD language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parts installation limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: As of the effective date of this AD, do not install the parts identified in paragraph (h)(1) or (2) of this AD on any helicopter unless the actions required by paragraph (g)(2) of this AD are accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibited-install parts include: (1) MGB P/N 332A32-5001-XX, 332A32-5002-XX, or 332A32-5003-XX with a main module and MOD 07-53016 (16-roller free wheel of free wheel shaft P/N 332A322191.20) installed (and P/N 332A32-5011-XX, 332A32-5012-XX, or 332A32-5013-XX), and (2) MGB P/N 332A32-5004-XX with main module P/N 332A32-5400-00.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit for previous actions per ASBs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides credit for the actions required by paragraphs (g)(1) and (2) of this AD, if those actions were performed before the effective date of this AD in accordance with specified Airbus Helicopters Emergency Alert Service Bulletins (ASBs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credit is given if work was done per: (1) ASB EC225-04A016 Revision 1, dated June 28, 2019; (2) ASB EC225-04A016 Revision 2, dated July 23, 2019; or (3) ASB EC225-04A016 Revision 3, dated August 5, 2019.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative Methods of Compliance (AMOCs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Manager, International Validation Branch, FAA, has the authority to approve AMOCs for this AD, if requested using the procedures found in 14 CFR 39.19.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit AMOC requests to your principal inspector or local Flight Standards District Office; or, if sending directly to the manager of the International Validation Branch, send to the person identified in paragraph (k)(1) of the AD and email to AMOC@faa.gov. Before using any approved AMOC, notify your appropriate principal inspector, or lacking one, the manager of the local flight standards district office/certificate holding district office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs of compliance estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated costs to comply with this proposed AD (labor $85 per hour).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determining the total hours TIS of each free wheel shaft: 0.25 work-hour, $21 per helicopter, $588 for U.S. fleet (28 helicopters). Installing placard(s) and revising RFM: 0.5 work-hour, $43 per helicopter, $1,204 for U.S. fleet. Replacing an MGB: 40 work-hours plus parts cost $850,000 (overhauled), estimated $853,400 per helicopter, per replacement cycle. Replacing the RH free wheel shaft: 4 work-hours plus parts $24,021, estimated $24,361 per helicopter, per replacement cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments due date
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAA must receive comments on this NPRM by July 7, 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: AD docket access and related material
rubrics_metrics.description: You may examine the AD docket at regulations.gov under Docket No. FAA—2025-0909; or in person at Docket Operations between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AD docket contains this NPRM, the mandatory continuing airworthiness information (MCAI), any comments received, and other information. For Airbus Helicopters material identified in this proposed AD, contact Airbus Helicopters (contact details provided in the NPRM).

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences between this proposed AD and the MCAI
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed AD includes differences from the MCAI (EASA action): it would require revising the existing RFM for the helicopter (whereas the MCAI does not), and the MCAI requires reporting while this proposed AD would not. The FAA also removed the requirement to determine the total hours TIS of the left-hand (LH) free wheel shaft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FAA determined additional affected parts and changed replacement and supervision requirements (e.g., repetitive replacement at the 1,000 TIS threshold and removal of the specified Airbus Helicopter Specialist requirement in favor of persons authorized under 14 CFR 43.3). The proposed AD is characterized as an interim action; further rulemaking may follow.
